newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mayors mull stadium bonds resolution.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mayors mull stadium bonds resolution.

text.p: U.S. mayors on Saturday will debate a resolution urging Congress not to curb tax-exempt financing of professional sports stadiums.

The U.S. Conference of Mayors resolution, submitted by the mayors of Dallas, New Orleans and Denver, asks Congress to oppose the "Stop Tax-Exempt Arena Debt Issuance Act" introduced by Sen. Daniel Patrick Moynihan, D-N.Y.
The resolution argues that the proposed legislation would represent a "dangerous precedent" for federal intrusion into the financial affairs of state and local governments.
"The cost to state and local taxpayers for building new sports facilities or rehabilitating existing ones would be dramatically increased or possibly become unaffordable," the resolution warned.

The resolution will be considered Saturday by the conference's Urban Economic Policy and Arts, Culture, and Recreation standing committees. If approved, the resolution would advance to the full conference for a vote on June 24.
Moynihan shook the municipal bond market when he introduced his bill, which would bar the use of tax-exempt government bonds to finance professional sports stadiums.
Opponents say the legislation would make public stadium financing almost impossible.
Earlier this year nine state and local government groups, including the Conference of Mayors, told Moynihan in a letter that his bill went too far.
